title: Magwinya: Doughnut Bites from Botswana
hookLine: Global-inspired magwinya: doughnut bites from botswana with 8 measured ingredients — zero sign-up, instant Cook Mode.

steps.title: Shape & Press Dough Evenly
steps.instructionTemplate: In a stand mixer bowl. add the water, sugar, and yeast. Leave to get foamy, about 5 minutes. Add in the flour, salt, and vegetable oil. Knead with a dough hook until a smooth dough forms, about 5 minutes. Incorporate {m53474_1}, {m53474_2}, {m53474_3}, and {m53474_4} smoothly until evenly distributed.
steps.creatorSecret: Prep and measure all purpose flour first—mise en place makes this dessert twice as fast.

steps.title: Fry Until Golden & Crisp
steps.instructionTemplate: Leave the dough to rise Remove the dough from the mixer bowl and form into a ball. Lightly mist the bowl with oil and replace the ball of dough into it. Cover the bowl and let rise in a warm place, 1 to 1½ hours, until doubled. Shape and fry the doughnuts. Incorporate {m53474_5}, {m53474_6}, {m53474_7}, and {m53474_8} smoothly until evenly distributed.

steps.title: Shape & Press Dough Evenly
steps.instructionTemplate: Preheat about 5cm (2") of vegetable oil in a pot to 180℃ / 350℉ – you can use a smaller pot needing less oil to fill but cooking less doughnuts at a time, or a larger one and cook more each batch. I also like to set up a drying rack set over a paper-towel-lined sheet pan to drain the doughnuts on, so they stay crispy. You can also prep a plate with paper towels if you don't want to bother. When the oil is at temperature, use a cookie scoop or two regular tablespoons to form a piece of dough into a rough ball shape and place in the oil. Repeat for as many doughnuts as will fit in your pot without overcrowding. Fry each doughnut for about a minute on each side, turning halfway through. Drain on prepared rack or paper towels.

steps.title: Drain Crisp, Garnish & Serve Warm
steps.instructionTemplate: When the doughnuts have cooled slightly, sprinkle with powdered sugar. Drain briefly on a wire cooling rack lined with paper towels for 1–2 minutes so the outside stays shatteringly crisp, then plate into 4 servings and enjoy warm.
steps.criticalTip: Let set for 5–10 minutes before slicing or plating so the textures hold crisp and photogenic!
steps.creatorSecret: Glaze or toss in sugar while still warm so the coating melts lightly and clings to every ridge.

ugcQuotes.quote: Followed the scaled metric steps—came out flawless in 33 mins!
